title: token-velocity-smokebench-suite
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our current microbench suites focus on peak sustained throughput but lack a compact, fast-to-run 'smoke' harness that simulates steady-state token velocity profiles across our core model catalog and surfaces p95 tail regressions quickly in CI. This ticket delivers a lightweight, reproducible token-velocity smokebench that complements heavier TPS CI jobs by providing rapid feedback on regressions affecting median tokens/sec and p95 latency for common batching/sequence-length shapes.

Scope:
- Implement a modular harness that runs O(10) short experiments per model variant (3-10s each) to estimate steady-state token/sec and p95.
- Support parameterized workloads: seq lengths {64, 128, 512}, batch sizes {1, 8, 32}, and KV-cache primed vs cold.
- Instrument to record tokens/sec (median), latency p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and tail jitter.
- Integrate a lightweight regression detector: compare current run to baseline using relative thresholds (>=10% TPS drop or >=15% increase in p95 triggers alert).
- Publish results to the CI dashboard and emit structured JSON artifacts for downstream trend analysis.
- Add a pluggable model adapter so new model variants can be onboarded without harness changes.

Deliverables: harness code + Docker image, CI job config, baseline artifact for core models, dashboard widgets, and a short runbook for triage steps when smokebench fails.
acceptance_criteria: Smokebench runs end-to-end under 10 minutes for the core catalog (5 models) on a single test GPU instance
Outputs structured JSON containing tokens_per_sec_median, lat_p50, lat_p95, gpu_util_pct, seq_len, batch_size, kv_cache_state for each experiment
Regression detector flags a run when TPS drops >=10% or p95 increases >=15%, with clear message and link to failing artifact
CI pipeline has a non-blocking smokebench stage that posts results to the performance dashboard and comments on the PR when thresholds are violated
Onboarding docs exist: how to add new model variants and adjust thresholds
steps: Design harness API and model adapter interface
Implement workload generator with configurable seq/batch/kv parameters
Add instrumentation hooks for tokens counting and latency histograms
Implement regression detector and baseline storage format
Create Docker image and CI job definition (non-blocking initially)
Wire results to performance dashboard and add dashboard widget for smokebench
Run smokebench against 5 core models and capture baseline artifacts

notes: Tradeoffs: we intentionally accept some measurement noise to keep runtime small — smokebench favors speed over statistical power. If a smokebench alert fires, the playbook should escalate to the longer sustained-throughput harness (ENG-7824/ENG-13580) for full repro and root-cause. Future work: auto-bisect across recent commits and correlate regressions with kernel / CUDA / quantization changes.
